why: The one most-general-dialect rule over the surfaces of ONE role that share a document: a whole-standard dialect `<kind>@<standard>/*` covers every subset dialect `<kind>@<standard>/<subset>` of its own kind and standard (every document of a subset of a standard is a document of the whole standard), and nothing else covers anything. The answer is the ONE candidate no other candidate covers; several uncovered candidates (whole-standard dialects of two standards, subsets without their whole standard, one dialect twice) are ambiguous and refused rather than resolved by order; no candidate answers none. Readers: the guest's `artifact_codec_owner` (which app of a bundle answers `codec.*` for a document schema, per role), the hub's creation selection (which editor creates a kind, within the deciding owner-or-host tier) and the hub's default document-open surface (which surface of a role opens a document when the client names none). `candidates` are canonical dialect coordinates (`ArtifactDialect::to_coordinate`); `mostGeneral` is the index of the answer, `ambiguous` or `none`.
liveDefects: Ticket 26/09/23 LB2 T7d p17, proof p17-s1 on 2026-09-29: the guest refused `codec.*` for the 13 document schemas that subset surfaces share with their whole-standard surface (stdio json, xml; image jpg, svg, tiff; cad dwg, step; bim ifc 2x3; pdf 1.7; office docx, pptx, xlsx; binary zip) with `artifact codec schema resolves more than one app of the same role`, so no host could create or register them.

Ticket 26/09/23 H14 on 2026-09-29: the hub's creation selection required exactly one editor per kind, so every multi-subset kind (json and xml owned by stdio; jpg, svg, tiff, step, docx, pptx, xlsx, zip, ifc and the semio kinds hosted by the stdio families) was never offered for creation, and a document opened without a requested surface (the semio MCP workspace) resolved no surface.
